summary: Follow-up testing of invite/esign/status-change iteration. 39/39 backend tests pass (11 new in TestInviteFlow, TestStatusEmails, TestEsign, TestBeneficiaryPctTotal). Frontend: Admin Invite client dialog, /accept-invite magic-link flow (redirects to intake wizard), and Send-for-Signing dialog on AdminCaseDetail all work. Backend logs show zero 'Resend send failed' during this iteration. E-sign correctly returns {enabled:false} and /send-for-signing returns 503 with clean message.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py admin_update_status: when an exception is thrown inside the status-email try/except block, logger.error is called with 'Status change email failed' but the backend still returns 200 — good behavior (email should not fail the API); confirmed correct.

server.py admin_send_for_signing: after Dropbox Sign upload, code mimics the status-change email manually (line ~1150). Works but duplicates _status_change_email logic — consider extracting a helper so invite/status/ready-for-signing all go through one function.

server.py resend email domain: at 20:26 UTC earlier today logs showed Resend 403 'You can only send testing emails to your own email address' — this is PRE-iteration and recipients during 22:52 test run (uitest_*@example.com, itest_*@example.com, testclient_*) appear to have been accepted by Resend (no errors in logs for this run). Domain DKIM status appears fully live now. Worth verifying in production that emails to arbitrary @example.com recipients are actually queued/delivered rather than silently dropped. Test recipients weren't inboxes we can check.

esign.py download_signed_pdf: uses api.signature_request_files which returns a urllib3 file-like — the fallback 'isinstance(resp, (bytes, bytearray))' may never hit in current SDK versions. Minor; low risk since e-sign is disabled.
InviteClientDialog.jsx uses native <select> not shadcn Select — consistent with rest of wizard; acceptable.
AcceptInvite.jsx successfully refresh()es auth context and navigates to /intake/{case_id} — verified end-to-end.
